cases.name: malformed-if
cases.description: An if= that does not parse

cases.name: undeclared-reference
cases.description: A ${{name}} naming no sequence would print literally

cases.name: unknown-filter
cases.description: An interpolation filter that does not exist

cases.name: each-on-a-scalar
cases.description: each= on a sequence that holds one value

cases.name: expression-nesting-past-the-ceiling
cases.description: 40 nested parentheses in if= — expression parsers recurse per level, so a runaway expression is refused at 32, not parsed until the stack gives out

cases.name: xml-entity-in-expression
cases.description: An XML entity in an expression: the config is XML-SHAPED but is not XML, so < stays four characters and the parser must say so rather than reporting the character it tripped over
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="P"><gen type="number" value="1..30"/></sequence><sequence name="T"><gen type="text" value="cheap" if="P <= 15"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-memory-at-scale
cases.description: uniq over a large run holds the whole column in memory. A <pool> has warned since TDC234; uniq costs the same and used to say nothing, and the run gave no clue why it needed half a gigabyte. The 250 bytes a value in the message is MEASURED, not guessed.

cases.name: unknown-function-in-an-if
cases.description: A typo in a function name, caught before the run. The suggestion comes from edit distance over the names that exist.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="text" value="5"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="abz(N) > 1" type="text" value="Y"/><gen type="text" value="N"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-planned-function-is-not-a-typo
cases.description: besselj is refused with the reason rather than a suggestion: edit distance would have offered "beta", an unrelated function. What is left on that list is the mathematics a data generator has no business carrying — Bessel, Airy, elliptic integrals, polygamma — each a project rather than a function. Everything a row predicate plausibly needs, including digamma, zeta and beta itself, IS implemented.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="text" value="5"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="besselj(N) > 1" type="text" value="Y"/><gen type="text" value="N"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-function-given-too-many-arguments
cases.description: Arity is checked by the validator, so a wrong call is a diagnostic with a position rather than a failure part-way through a run.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="text" value="5"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="abs(N, 2) > 1" type="text" value="Y"/><gen type="text" value="N"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-list-standing-on-its-own
cases.description: A list is a set of values to test against, so it means something only to the right of `in`. On its own there is no value for the condition to be.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="text" value="5"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="[1, 2]" type="text" value="Y"/><gen type="text" value="N"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: at-on-a-value-that-was-never-split
cases.description: A repeat list reaches an expression as its JOINED text, so at(Items, 1) asks for the second element of a one-element list. It answered with the same empty string a legitimately short row gives, so the run reported success and the column came out blank. A name can never hold a list, which makes this provable from the text alone.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="Items"><gen type="text" value="5" repeat="3" separator=","/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="at(Items, 1) == 5" type="text" value="Y"/><gen type="text" value="N"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: an-index-that-is-not-an-index
cases.description: An index is a whole number, zero or more. Past the end of a list IS empty text, deliberately, because repeat="1..4" makes rows of different lengths — but -1 is a mistake in the config, not a shape the data can take, and it used to answer with that same empty string.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="Items"><gen type="text" value="5" repeat="3" separator=","/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="at(split(Items, ','), -1) == 5" type="text" value="Y"/><gen type="text" value="N"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-stray-semicolon-after-an-expression
cases.description: `if="A ;"` is not a condition. The reference used to ACCEPT it and run the config: it hands expressions to a parser library that drops a trailing separator and returns the expression before it, so the stray character vanished without a word while all four ports refused the same file. One sentence for the shape now, in all five.

cases.name: two-expressions-side-by-side
cases.description: `if="A B"` — two expressions with no operator between them. The reference used to report the parser library's own name for the node, `unsupported expression construct "Compound"`, which names an internal detail rather than the mistake.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="A"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence></env><block><line if="A B"><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: an-entity-explains-it-before-the-shape-does
cases.description: `if="A > 5"` trips two different parsers in two different places — one reads it as two expressions, the other stops at the leftover — but it is ONE mistake with one cause, so the entity is named first in all five.
